HDFC Bank announced Q2FY27 results

Standalone Financial Highlights:

  • Total Income: Reached Rs 97,267.62 crore in Q2FY27, reflecting a YoY increase of 6.84% from Rs 91,040.72 crore in Q2FY26, and a QoQ increase of 5.51% from Rs 92,184.38 crore in Q1FY27. For H1FY27, the total income was Rs 1,89,442.00 crore.
  • Net Revenue: Stood at Rs 484.5 billion for Q2FY27, reporting a 5.5% YoY growth compared to Rs 459.0 billion in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, net revenues were Rs 948.1 billion.
  • Net Interest Income (NII): Grew by 9.7% YoY to Rs 346.2 billion in Q2FY27 from Rs 315.5 billion in Q2FY26. The Net Interest Margin for the quarter was 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets.
  • Other Income: Reported at Rs 13,831.02 crore in Q2FY27 (Rs 138.3 billion as per the press release). Key components included fees & commissions of Rs 96.9 billion, miscellaneous income (including recoveries and dividends) of Rs 18.1 billion, foreign exchange & derivatives revenue of Rs 15.5 billion, and treasury trading gains of Rs 7.8 billion.
  • Operating Profit (Before provisions and contingencies): Achieved Rs 29,483.42 crore in Q2FY27, up 5.59% YoY from Rs 27,923.60 crore in Q2FY26, and up 4.67% QoQ from Rs 28,168.06 crore in Q1FY27.
  • Net Profit (PAT): Reached Rs 19,509.96 crore for Q2FY27 (Rs 195.1 billion as per the press release), registering a 4.66% YoY growth from Rs 18,641.28 crore in Q2FY26, and a 2.31% QoQ growth from Rs 19,069.72 crore in Q1FY27. Excluding treasury trading gains, PAT grew by approximately 12.6% YoY. For H1FY27, PAT stood at Rs 38,669.68 crore.

Consolidated Financial Highlights:

  • Total Income: Reported at Rs 1,29,358.69 crore in Q2FY27, representing a YoY growth of 9.11% against Rs 1,18,560.63 crore in Q2FY26, but reflecting a QoQ decline of 2.82% from Rs 1,33,110.36 crore in Q1FY27.
  • Net Revenue: Reached Rs 786.9 billion for Q2FY27.
  • Profit Before Tax (PBT): Stood at Rs 28,662.54 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 7.51% YoY increase from Rs 26,658.89 crore in Q2FY26 and a 5.40% QoQ increase from Rs 27,193.16 crore in Q1FY27.
  • Net Profit (PAT after minority interest): Achieved Rs 20,700.03 crore in Q2FY27 (Rs 207.0 billion as per the press release), increasing by 5.55% YoY from Rs 19,610.67 crore in Q2FY26 and by 7.56% QoQ from Rs 19,244.71 crore in Q1FY27. For H1FY27, consolidated PAT stood at Rs 39,944.74 crore.

Business Highlights:

  • Balance Sheet: Total balance sheet size expanded to Rs 45,778 billion as of Q2FY27, highlighting a 14.36% YoY growth from Rs 40,030 billion in Q2FY26.

## ABOUT THE REPORT
The Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 presents comprehensive overview of HDFC Bank's (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank;' we; and "our") approach to delivering long term value for all its stakeholders including customers, shareholders, regulators, employees, investors, and the larger community: In addition to the annual financial performance, the report highlights the Bank's progress on strategic priorities, sustainability initiatives, and non financial performance. It details the Bank's operating context; disciplined risk management; robust governance practices, and the ESG focus areas that steer decision making and value creation. The report showcases the initiatives that foster a people-first culture, accelerate innovation-driven technology adoption, and strengthen execution excellence, all of which underpin consistent; sustainable growth. "us;
## REPORTING PRINCIPLES AND FRAMEWORK
The financial information presented in this report is in line with the requirements of
- The Companies Act; 2013 (including the rules made thereunder)
- The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
- The Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021
- The Banking Regulation Act; 1949 and other relevant Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations
The preparation of this report draws on the principles of the Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework issued by the IFRS Foundation and incorporates disclosures aligned with leading standards and frameworks. These include the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards (2021), the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) requirements, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs):
During the reporting period, the Bank has not revised or restated any information presented in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.
## MATERIALITY AND SCOPE
This report presents information relevant to all stakeholders and offers a comprehensive view of the Bank's operations and performance: It highlights topics that meaningfully influence the Bank's capacity to generate long-term value and may inform the decisions of providers of financial capital.
In FY 2025-26, the Bank undertook a review of its material matters through a double materiality assessment in line with the GRI Universal Standards 2021. Details of the GRI-aligned topics and corresponding disclosures are available in the GRI Content Index included within this report: This reassessment considered both the impact of the Bank's operations and value chain on the environment and society, and the impact of the external operating environment; including regulatory expectations, emerging industry developments, and the evolving risk landscape, on the Bank's financial performance
Refer to the 'Materiality' section on Page 66 for more information
## REPORTING BOUNDARY
The non-financial disclosures in this report present the Bank's activities and performance on a standalone basis for the period of April 1,2025,to March 31,2026. Unless otherwise stated, the sustainability disclosures presented in this report cover HDFC Bank Limited and all operations under the Bank's operational control: The previous edition of the report covered the period April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025. The Integrated Report for FY 2024-25 is available for reference here\_
## ASSURANCE STATEMENT
Reasonable assurance on the BRSR Core KPIs and limited assurance on select indicators presented in the BRSR and the Integrated Annual Report has been undertaken by SGS India Pvt: Ltd. The assurance engagement was carried out in accordance with ISAE 3000 (Revised) and ISAE 3410. The assurance statements included in this report have been prepared in line with SEBI's BRSR Core Framework for assurance, BRSR Reporting Guidelines and the Greenhouse Gas Protocol standards. The statements outline the scope of review; assessment criteria, procedures performed, and the resulting reasonable assurance opinion or limited assurance conclusion, as applicable
## RESPONSIBILITY STATEMENT
The content presented in this report has undergone review by the Bank's senior management and has been formally reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors This process ensures that the information disclosed is accurate, complete, and aligned with the principles and requirements of the Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework:

news.headline: Q2FY27 Quarterly Result Announced for HDFC Bank Ltd.
news.description: HDFC Bank announced Q2FY27 results Standalone Financial Highlights:  Total Income: Reached Rs 97,267.62 crore in Q2FY27, reflecting a YoY increase of 6.84% from Rs 91,040.72 crore in Q2FY26, and a QoQ increase of 5.51% from Rs 92,184.38 crore in Q1FY27. For H1FY27, the total income was Rs 1,89,442.00 crore. Net Revenue: Stood at Rs 484.5 billion for Q2FY27, reporting a 5.5% YoY growth compared to Rs 459.0 billion in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, net revenues were Rs 948.1 billion. Net Interest Income (NII): Grew by 9.7% YoY to Rs 346.2 billion in Q2FY27 from Rs 315.5 billion in Q2FY26. The Net Interest Margin for the quarter was 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets. Other Income: Reported at Rs 13,831.02 crore in Q2FY27 (Rs 138.3 billion as per the press release). Key components included fees & commissions of Rs 96.9 billion, miscellaneous income (including recoveries and dividends) of Rs 18.1 billion, foreign exchange & derivatives revenue of Rs 15.5 billion, and treasury trading gains of Rs 7.8 billion. Operating Profit (Before provisions and contingencies): Achieved Rs 29,483.42 crore in Q2FY27, up 5.59% YoY from Rs 27,923.60 crore in Q2FY26, and up 4.67% QoQ from Rs 28,168.06 crore in Q1FY27. Net Profit (PAT): Reached Rs 19,509.96 crore for Q2FY27 (Rs 195.1 billion as per the press release), registering a 4.66% YoY growth from Rs 18,641.28 crore in Q2FY26, and a 2.31% QoQ growth from Rs 19,069.72 crore in Q1FY27. Excluding treasury trading gains, PAT grew by approximately 12.6% YoY. For H1FY27, PAT stood at Rs 38,669.68 crore.  Consolidated Financial Highlights:  Total Income: Reported at Rs 1,29,358.69 crore in Q2FY27, representing a YoY growth of 9.11% against Rs 1,18,560.63 crore in Q2FY26, but reflecting a QoQ decline of 2.82% from Rs 1,33,110.36 crore in Q1FY27. Net Revenue: Reached Rs 786.9 billion for Q2FY27. Profit Before Tax (PBT): Stood at Rs 28,662.54 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 7.51% YoY increase from Rs 26,658.89 crore in Q2FY26 and a 5.40% QoQ increase from Rs 27,193.16 crore in Q1FY27. Net Profit (PAT after minority interest): Achieved Rs 20,700.03 crore in Q2FY27 (Rs 207.0 billion as per the press release), increasing by 5.55% YoY from Rs 19,610.67 crore in Q2FY26 and by 7.56% QoQ from Rs 19,244.71 crore in Q1FY27. For H1FY27, consolidated PAT stood at Rs 39,944.74 crore.  Business Highlights:  Balance Sheet: Total balance sheet size expanded to Rs 45,778 billion as of Q2FY27, highlighting a 14.36% YoY growth from Rs 40,030 billion in Q2FY26. Deposits: Total EOP Deposits were Rs 33,274 billion as of Q2FY27, increasing by 18.8% YoY. Average deposits were Rs 31,664 billion, witnessing a 16.8% YoY growth and a 5.1% QoQ increase. CASA: Average CASA deposits stood at Rs 9,712 billion in Q2FY27, growing by 10.7% YoY and 1.5% QoQ. CASA deposits made up 31.6% of the total deposits. Advances: Gross advances stood at Rs 32,195 billion as of Q2FY27, reflecting an increase of 16.3% YoY. Advances under management grew by 15.3% YoY. Asset Quality: Gross NPAs improved sequentially to 1.11% of gross advances in Q2FY27 compared to 1.17% in Q1FY27 and 1.24% in Q2FY26. Net NPAs declined to 0.37% of net advances in Q2FY27, against 0.41% in Q1FY27 and 0.42% in Q2FY26. Capital Adequacy: Total Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) as per Basel III guidelines stood at 18.9% as of Q2FY27 (compared to 20.0% in Q2FY26). Tier 1 CAR was 17.2%. Network footprint: The bank expanded its network to 9,706 branches and 20,881 ATMs across 4,177 cities/towns in Q2FY27, compared to 9,545 branches and 21,417 ATMs in Q2FY26.  Segment-wise Performance:  Retail Banking: Reached Rs 79,112.16 crore in Q2FY27, marking a 4.67% YoY growth from Rs 75,584.52 crore in Q2FY26 and a 4.25% QoQ growth from Rs 75,888.80 crore in Q1FY27. Under this, retail loan portfolios grew by 11.7% YoY. Wholesale Banking: Recorded at Rs 52,743.87 crore in Q2FY27, translating to an impressive 24.66% YoY increase from Rs 42,308.37 crore in Q2FY26 and an 8.37% QoQ increase from Rs 48,670.85 crore in Q1FY27. Under this, corporate and other wholesale loans grew by 16.4% YoY. Treasury: Stood at Rs 19,150.30 crore in Q2FY27, a 7.08% YoY decline from Rs 20,609.22 crore in Q2FY26, but a 5.27% QoQ increase from Rs 18,192.38 crore in Q1FY27. Other Banking Operations: Posted Rs 9,700.20 crore in Q2FY27, marking a 3.93% YoY growth from Rs 9,333.81 crore in Q2FY26 and a 7.25% QoQ increase from Rs 9,044.03 crore in Q1FY27. Key Subsidiaries Performance:  HDB Financial Services Ltd (HDBFSL): Net revenue recorded at Rs 31.9 billion. PAT stood at Rs 7.8 billion, showcasing a 34.2% YoY growth from Rs 5.8 billion in Q2FY26. HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd: PAT achieved Rs 5.1 billion, growing by 13.6% YoY compared to Rs 4.5 billion in Q2FY26. HDFC Securities Ltd (HSL): Total revenue grew to Rs 9.6 billion. PAT reached Rs 2.7 billion, demonstrating a 26.1% YoY growth against Rs 2.1 billion in Q2FY26. HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd (HDFC AMC): PAT registered at Rs 7.5 billion, higher than the Rs 7.2 billion reported in Q2FY26. HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Ltd: PAT came in at Rs 1.6 billion, sliding down from the Rs 1.8 billion posted in Q2FY26.    Result PDF

## ABOUT THE REPORT
The Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 presents comprehensive overview of HDFC Bank's (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank;' we; and "our") approach to delivering long term value for all its stakeholders including customers, shareholders, regulators, employees, investors, and the larger community: In addition to the annual financial performance, the report highlights the Bank's progress on strategic priorities, sustainability initiatives, and non financial performance. It details the Bank's operating context; disciplined risk management; robust governance practices, and the ESG focus areas that steer decision making and value creation. The report showcases the initiatives that foster a people-first culture, accelerate innovation-driven technology adoption, and strengthen execution excellence, all of which underpin consistent; sustainable growth. "us;
## REPORTING PRINCIPLES AND FRAMEWORK
The financial information presented in this report is in line with the requirements of
- The Companies Act; 2013 (including the rules made thereunder)
- The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
- The Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021
- The Banking Regulation Act; 1949 and other relevant Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations
The preparation of this report draws on the principles of the Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework issued by the IFRS Foundation and incorporates disclosures aligned with leading standards and frameworks. These include the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards (2021), the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) requirements, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs):
During the reporting period, the Bank has not revised or restated any information presented in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.
## MATERIALITY AND SCOPE
This report presents information relevant to all stakeholders and offers a comprehensive view of the Bank's operations and performance: It highlights topics that meaningfully influence the Bank's capacity to generate long-term value and may inform the decisions of providers of financial capital.
In FY 2025-26, the Bank undertook a review of its material matters through a double materiality assessment in line with the GRI Universal Standards 2021. Details of the GRI-aligned topics and corresponding disclosures are available in the GRI Content Index included within this report: This reassessment considered both the impact of the Bank's operations and value chain on the environment and society, and the impact of the external operating environment; including regulatory expectations, emerging industry developments, and the evolving risk landscape, on the Bank's financial performance
Refer to the 'Materiality' section on Page 66 for more information
## REPORTING BOUNDARY
The non-financial disclosures in this report present the Bank's activities and performance on a standalone basis for the period of April 1,2025,to March 31,2026. Unless otherwise stated, the sustainability disclosures presented in this report cover HDFC Bank Limited and all operations under the Bank's operational control: The previous edition of the report covered the period April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025. The Integrated Report for FY 2024-25 is available for reference here\_
## ASSURANCE STATEMENT
Reasonable assurance on the BRSR Core KPIs and limited assurance on select indicators presented in the BRSR and the Integrated Annual Report has been undertaken by SGS India Pvt: Ltd. The assurance engagement was carried out in accordance with ISAE 3000 (Revised) and ISAE 3410. The assurance statements included in this report have been prepared in line with SEBI's BRSR Core Framework for assurance, BRSR Reporting Guidelines and the Greenhouse Gas Protocol standards. The statements outline the scope of review; assessment criteria, procedures performed, and the resulting reasonable assurance opinion or limited assurance conclusion, as applicable
## RESPONSIBILITY STATEMENT
The content presented in this report has undergone review by the Bank's senior management and has been formally reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors This process ensures that the information disclosed is accurate, complete, and aligned with the principles and requirements of the Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework:
## GOVERNANCE OVER INTEGRATED REPORTING PROCESS

## ABOUT THE REPORT
The Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 presents comprehensive overview of HDFC Bank's (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank;' we; and "our") approach to delivering long term value for all its stakeholders including customers, shareholders, regulators, employees, investors, and the larger community: In addition to the annual financial performance, the report highlights the Bank's progress on strategic priorities, sustainability initiatives, and non financial performance. It details the Bank's operating context; disciplined risk management; robust governance practices, and the ESG focus areas that steer decision making and value creation. The report showcases the initiatives that foster a people-first culture, accelerate innovation-driven technology adoption, and strengthen execution excellence, all of which underpin consistent; sustainable growth. ## REPORTING PRINCIPLES AND FRAMEWORK
The financial information presented in this report is in line with the requirements of
- The Companies Act; 2013 (including the rules made thereunder)
- The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
- The Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021
- The Banking Regulation Act; 1949 and other relevant Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations
The preparation of this report draws on the principles of the Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework issued by the IFRS Foundation and incorporates disclosures aligned with leading standards and frameworks. These include the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards (2021), the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations, the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) requirements, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs):
During the reporting period, the Bank has not revised or restated any information presented in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.
## MATERIALITY AND SCOPE
This report presents information relevant to all stakeholders and offers a comprehensive view of the Bank's operations and performance: It highlights topics that meaningfully influence the Bank's capacity to generate long-term value and may inform the decisions of providers of financial capital.
In FY 2025-26, the Bank undertook a review of its material matters through a double materiality assessment in line with the GRI Universal Standards 2021. Details of the GRI-aligned topics and corresponding disclosures are available in the GRI Content Index included within this report: This reassessment considered both the impact of the Bank's operations and value chain on the environment and society, and the impact of the external operating environment; including regulatory expectations, emerging industry developments, and the evolving risk landscape, on the Bank's financial performance
Refer to the 'Materiality' section on Page 66 for more information
## REPORTING BOUNDARY
The non-financial disclosures in this report present the Bank's activities and performance on a standalone basis for the period of April 1,2025,to March 31,2026. Unless otherwise stated, the sustainability disclosures presented in this report cover HDFC Bank Limited and all operations under the Bank's operational control: The previous edition of the report covered the period April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025. ## MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
## MACROECONOMIC AND INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENTS
The Indian economy demonstrated resilience during the Financial Year 2025-26 despite an increasingly uncertain global environment marked by trade-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions and volatility in financial markets: India's GDP is estimated to have grown by 7.7 per cent during the Financial Year 2025-26, compared to 7.1 per cent in the previous fiscal year; supported by strong domestic demand conditions, easing inflationary pressures, accommodative monetary policy, and sustained public investment: GST rate cuts during the third quarter of the year added further impetus to consumer demand:
Economic activity remained broad-based across sectors with continued momentum in manufacturing; construction, and services. Manufacturing activity benefited from improving domestic demand and export-related production, while the construction sector continued to be supported by government infrastructure spending and healthy real estate activity. The services sector remained a driver of growth, aided by strong demand across financial, digital, travel, and business services Agricultural output and rural demand conditions also remained favourable during the year, supported by anormal monsoon and improved farm sector activity: key "
Inflationary pressures moderated significantly during FY 202526, with headline retail inflation averaging 2.1 per cent during the year: Lower food inflation, easing supply-side pressures; and indirect tax reductions contributed to the moderation in prices The RBI continued to support growth during FY 2025-26 through monetary easing measures amid moderating inflation conditions reducing the policy rate to 5.25 per cent:
The banking sector continued to witness healthy balance sheet trends during FY 2025-26. With an easing in interest rates and rise in consumer demand, credit growth rose to 14.1 per cent led by strong momentum in retail and MSME loans: Asset quality across the banking sector continued to improve, with gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratios remaining near multiyear lows of 2.15 per cent as of September 2025, supported by stronger provisioning buffers, recoveries, and improved underwriting standards:

Inflationary pressures moderated significantly during FY 202526, with headline retail inflation averaging 2.1 per cent during the year: Lower food inflation, easing supply-side pressures; and indirect tax reductions contributed to the moderation in prices The RBI continued to support growth during FY 2025-26 through monetary easing measures amid moderating inflation conditions reducing the policy rate to 5.25 per cent:
The banking sector continued to witness healthy balance sheet trends during FY 2025-26. With an easing in interest rates and rise in consumer demand, credit growth rose to 14.1 per cent led by strong momentum in retail and MSME loans: Asset quality across the banking sector continued to improve, with gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratios remaining near multiyear lows of 2.15 per cent as of September 2025, supported by stronger provisioning buffers, recoveries, and improved underwriting standards:
